requirements.title: AI+D advanced undergraduate elective
requirements.summary: Choose one listed advanced subject; the chart gives 12–15 units for this slot.

requirements.title: Social and ethical responsibilities of computing
requirements.summary: Satisfy at least one program requirement or elective using a listed SERC-qualified subject; this is an overlay, not necessarily an additional course.

requirements.title: Additional Course 6 or 18 elective
requirements.summary: The unversioned chart permits one subject satisfying a Course 6 or Course 18 degree requirement, with a 12–15-unit slot. This is a published eligibility criterion. The department’s 6-4_2025 version separately specifies named EECS/graduate pools and an open MATH criterion; the two source scopes are not silently equated.

requirements.title: Second CI-M subject
requirements.summary: The unversioned chart requires a second CI-M subject beyond the application choice. A named CIM2 pool has now been verified for the department’s explicit 6-4_2025 version; applicability differences between that version and the catalog chart remain unresolved.

requirements.title: SERC module credit condition
requirements.summary: Credit for 6.C01 requires completion of a 6-unit disciplinary module; consult an advisor. Do not treat its listed 6 units as sufficient by itself.

requirements.title: General Institute Requirements
requirements.summary: The chart summarizes 17 GIR subjects: six science, eight HASS (at least two CI-H), two REST (identified as 6.1200 and 18.C06), and one laboratory requirement (identified as 6.1010, 12 units). Detailed distributions and choice pools remain unreviewed.

requirements.title: Physical education and swimming
requirements.summary: The Course 6-4 chart summarizes swimming plus four physical-education courses for eight points. The institute GIR source separately provides the transfer-entry reduction and other completion paths; see its linked policy note.

requirements.title: Major, GIR overlap and degree accounting
requirements.summary: The chart reports 168–177 major units, 36 major units also satisfying GIRs, and 180–189 units beyond the GIRs. Units for any of the 17 GIR subjects cannot also count toward units required beyond the GIRs. Ranges are preserved, not replaced with a fabricated single total.

requirements.title: Linked general CI-M reference list
requirements.summary: The degree chart links this general EECS CI-M list, but the page does not identify a CIM2 subset. These course observations are a reference pool, not a verified set of second-CI-M choices for Course 6-4.

requirements.title: Minimum attendance and approved program
requirements.summary: Attend at least three regular academic terms, ordinarily including the graduation term, and complete an approved GIR and departmental program. Departmental deviations need department permission; GIR substitutions require the appropriate faculty-committee petition.

requirements.title: Transfer cohort requirements
requirements.summary: Transfer students normally follow requirements for the class they join on entry; the source does not assign an entry year to this program record.

requirements.title: Units beyond GIRs
requirements.summary: At least 48 unrestricted elective units belong within the program-specific units beyond GIRs. ROTC units are excluded. CI-M units generally count beyond GIRs, except when that subject also supplies one of the 17 GIR subjects. Use the Course 6-4 chart for its specific unit range.

requirements.title: Calculus advanced credit
requirements.summary: Existing AP, advanced-standing or transfer credit for 18.01 is lost on taking 18.01; taking 18.01A instead earns three elective units. Placement and subject-specific calculus policies require the linked mathematics guidance.

requirements.title: Physics sequencing and advanced credit
requirements.summary: A Physics I GIR credit must precede enrollment in a Physics II GIR subject, even when mixing sequences. Students with AP or advanced-standing 8.01 credit who take 8.012 receive six elective units in place of 8.01.

requirements.title: Communication totals and annual pace
requirements.summary: Complete two CI-H/HW and two major-specific CI-M subjects. Minimum cumulative progress is one by year one, two by year two, three by year three and four by graduation. Only one CI-H per term counts, while multiple CI-M or a concurrent CI-H and CI-M may count. Noncompliance is referred to academic-performance review.

requirements.title: First communication subject placement
requirements.summary: The first CI subject must be CI-HW unless the First-year Essay Evaluation permits CI-H/CI-HW, AP English Language or Literature is 5, or higher-level IB English A/B is 7. An eligible student may still choose CI-HW. Pass the first CI-H/HW by the end of the second term.

requirements.title: Communication for double majors
requirements.summary: Double majors must meet the CI-M component of each major plus two CI-H subjects. Four CI-M subjects are normal; a subject common to both departments may satisfy both when permitted.

requirements.title: HASS minimum and distribution criteria
requirements.summary: Complete eight HASS-designated subjects, including one from each distribution category: humanities, arts and social sciences. Two CI-H/HW subjects may simultaneously meet communication requirements. Eligibility is defined by official designation; this rule does not invent a fixed course list.

requirements.title: HASS concentration and deadlines
requirements.summary: Complete a field-specific three- or four-subject HASS concentration with its designated advisor. Submit the proposal by the end of the first week of the second junior-year term and completion form by the end of the first week of the final graduation term. One distribution subject may overlap with advisor permission. A special concentration needs advance approval; field-specific rules remain unreviewed.

requirements.title: Remaining HASS eligibility
requirements.summary: After distribution and concentration, remaining slots in the eight-subject total may use subjects in any HASS distribution category or designated HASS electives.

requirements.title: REST selection and departmental restriction
requirements.summary: Complete two REST-designated subjects, ordinarily no more than one from the student’s department; jointly offered J subjects are exempt from that departmental limit. Departmental degree subjects may simultaneously satisfy REST. Course 6-4 identifies 6.1200[J] and 18.C06[J] as its normal route; substitutions require review.

requirements.title: Laboratory-designated credit
requirements.summary: Complete 12 units specifically designated as Institute Laboratory credit; subjects may be combined, and designated laboratory credit can differ from total subject units. Subject units above the 12 needed count beyond GIRs. Course 6-4 identifies 6.1010 as its normal route.

requirements.title: PE, transfer and swimming paths
requirements.summary: First-year entrants complete four PE/wellness courses for eight points; transfer entrants complete two courses for four points. Both must satisfy swimming through a beginning swim class or test. Each varsity year earns four points; each ROTC year earns two, capped at four. Approved training/swim/exercise options may earn points. Finish by the end of year two or submit an extension plan. PE points are not academic units.

requirements.title: Undergraduate academic-performance review
requirements.summary: The CAP normally accepts at least 36 units per regular term with a term rating above 3.0/5, unless it has imposed a higher individual standard. Falling below this triggers individual review rather than an automatic graduation GPA cutoff. The cumulative 3.0 federal-aid criterion is a separate financial-aid rule.

requirements.title: Passing and nonpassing grades
requirements.summary: D is generally passing, but a department may require additional work or repetition before the next subject. Authorized P corresponds to A–C performance; first-year DN/FN do not earn credit. Exact first-year and flexible P/NR eligibility remains subject to separate policy review.

requirements.title: Incomplete grades at graduation
requirements.summary: Resolve ordinary I grades before graduation, and no ordinary I can be assigned in the graduation term. The exceptional emergency IE notation carries no credit but need not be resolved before graduation; the source distinguishes these cases.

requirements.title: Degree application and clearance
requirements.summary: Submit the SB degree application by the relevant academic-calendar deadline. Award requires faculty approval following committee/department recommendation, cleared financial obligations and no pending disciplinary actions.

requirements.title: Department declaration availability
requirements.summary: The department says students could declare Course 6-4 beginning Fall 2022. This is declaration evidence, not proof of the first instructional offering or of the applicable curriculum version.

requirements.title: Departmental substitutions and petitions
requirements.summary: Discuss a proposed substitution with the advisor, then submit a departmental petition for advisor comments and department action. Decisions are individual, never automatically guaranteed by another student’s approval. Submit early, including before taking a proposed substitute, rather than waiting until the final semester. The student-specific audit is restricted to current EECS students and is not part of this public-source inventory.

requirements.title: Version 6-4_2025 applicability
requirements.summary: The public department source labels this version 6-4_2025, requires it for students entering MIT in Fall 2025 or later, and says subject lists are current as of Fall 2026. Those labels are curriculum applicability evidence, not a first-offered date or an inferred catalog edition.

requirements.title: Version 6-4_2025: subject reuse
requirements.summary: Each completed subject may fill at most one required subject slot but may satisfy multiple additional constraints, including center, SERC and CIM2 designations. Do not impose separate unique subjects for every overlay.

requirements.title: Version 6-4_2025: open mathematics elective criterion
requirements.summary: The MATH option permits any non-calculus subject satisfying a Course 18 SB requirement, provided its content is not essentially similar to other subjects counted toward this degree. This is an eligibility criterion, not a fabricated finite list.

requirements.title: EECS option-pool eligibility
requirements.summary: The EECS list describes subjects meeting departmental undergraduate requirements in Courses 6-1 through 6-5, excluding subjects of six units or fewer. Printed bundles remain whole options. Separate graduate lists supply additional expressly allowed routes; listing does not waive subject prerequisites.

requirements.title: HASS units and grading
requirements.summary: Complete eight HASS subjects normally carrying at least nine units each, using letter grades or authorized first-year/flexible P/NR. AP credit cannot fulfill any HASS component. Approved six-unit combinations are separate exceptions.

requirements.title: External HASS credit restrictions
requirements.summary: External transfer/cross-registered work is generally HASS Elective credit only; the HASS policy excludes external Distribution credit, Pass/Fail subjects and Harvard Law subjects. The separate transfer-processing page mentions a Distribution award case; that wording conflict requires office clarification, not an inferred automatic exception.

requirements.title: HASS substitution eligibility and approval
requirements.summary: A nondesignated subject needs HASS-subcommittee approval and an authorized grading basis. Letter-graded Harvard/Wellesley subjects, SHASS graduate subjects and approved six-unit combinations may qualify; UROPs, internships, independent studies, Pass/Fail or P/D/F work and Harvard Law subjects do not. Obtain advisor approval and, for a graduate subject, the instructor signature.

requirements.title: Six-unit classical-language combinations
requirements.summary: By petition, one HASS Humanities or Elective subject can be formed from a complete Latin pair 21L.611+21L.612 or 21L.613+21L.614, or Greek pair 21L.607+21L.608 or 21L.609+21L.610. These are conditional combination rules, not additional degree course slots.

requirements.title: Six-unit performance and literature combinations
requirements.summary: Up to four six-unit Music/Theater performance or sampling subjects can form two 12-unit HASS subjects. Up to four six-unit literature samplings can form two HASS subjects, excluding 21L.340. Arts/Humanities Distribution combinations audit automatically as applicable; using a combination for HASS Elective credit needs an office audit adjustment.

requirements.title: HASS concentration plan and revision
requirements.summary: Choose a listed HASS field and an advisor-approved three- or four-subject plan. A concentration and minor may share a field. Outside subjects require both transfer examiner and concentration-advisor approval; one Distribution overlap requires the advisor. Revise subjects with the advisor and form; a field change requires notifying the former advisor and submitting a new form. Specific field rules remain conditional on the selected field.

requirements.title: CI passing and ordering conditions
requirements.summary: CI credit requires passing the designated subject. A CI-HW-required student gets no CI credit for an earlier CI subject taken before the required writing subject. Failure to maintain communication pace can lead to a CAP warning and next-term credit limit.

requirements.title: Communication transfer route
requirements.summary: Transfer entrants take the FEE and pass or obtain approved transfer credit for a CI subject in their first MIT year. Transfer CI credit needs department-examiner approval followed by a communication-subcommittee petition. Two CI-H and two CI-M credits are still required by graduation.

requirements.title: Communication exceptions and double-major reuse
requirements.summary: Petition the communication subcommittee for a CI-M outside the major or a CI-M serving two majors. An outside CI-M needs a coherent advisor-approved plan. Pace deferral is rarely approved except after a major change; an appeal requires substantial new information. No exception is automatic.

requirements.title: FEE-specific first writing route
requirements.summary: Without an FEE result or valid exemption, placement defaults to CI-HW required. If placed into 21W.222, it must precede any other CI credit. A 21W.220 recommendation is preparation, earns HASS-H but no CI credit, and does not replace required 21W.222. AP English 5 or English A/B higher-level IB 7 provides the stated FEE exemption.

requirements.title: First-year grading and credit
requirements.summary: First-year fall and IAP use P/NR; spring uses A/B/C/No Record before standard grading from sophomore year. P requires C- or better; D/F become No Record and earn no credit. Fall 2020+ entrants may use the separate 48-unit flexible P/NR allowance after their first term.

requirements.title: Flexible P/NR credit and designation
requirements.summary: After the first term, up to 48 units may use flexible P/NR, including GIR and departmental requirements; advanced-standing-exam grades cannot. P requires C- or better; D/F earn no credit. Choose after final grades and before the next enrolled regular-term Add Date; final-term seniors have until the day before CAP degree meetings. Late changes or reversal are normally not permitted.

requirements.title: Repeat credit and GPA
requirements.summary: Repeated subjects normally earn unit credit once, unless explicitly designated repeatable for credit. Both grades remain on internal/external records and enter term/cumulative GPA calculations using the normal units for each attempt.

requirements.title: External transfer eligibility and accounting
requirements.summary: Department examiners decide equivalence, elective credit and any minimum grade; consult before external enrollment and provide an official transcript. Transfer credit uses S, counts toward approved requirements and does not enter GPA. Work used for another institution’s awarded degree cannot transfer. HASS and CI require additional approval.

requirements.title: Unresolved external HASS Distribution wording
requirements.summary: The transfer-processing page describes final HASS signature handling when an examiner awards Distribution credit, whereas the HASS requirement/substitution pages disallow external Distribution credit. Preserve this administrative source conflict and seek HASS-office clarification before treating it as an exception. All CI transfer credit requires communication-subcommittee approval.

requirements.title: Advanced-standing examination eligibility
requirements.summary: An ASE needs advisor/registration-officer and instructor/department approval. Cross-registered and special students are ineligible. Prior attendance or registration in the subject or a variation normally disqualifies the attempt; the exception requires never attending and dropping within the first week. A failed ASE cannot be repeated, though the subject may subsequently be taken.

requirements.title: ASE credit, GPA and first-year timing
requirements.summary: Passing an ASE earns full subject credit but its grade does not enter GPA; a subsequent enrolled attempt enters GPA and both records remain visible. ASE grades cannot use flexible P/NR. For first-year students, fall ASE C-or-better is P, spring passing grades are A/B/C; nonpassing-record visibility depends on timing. December/May ASE units count toward first-year or academic-warning term limits, unlike August/September or January/February. Published first-year regular-term limits are 54 plus six FYD units in fall and 60 plus six FYD in spring; IAP ASE units do not count toward its 12-unit limit.

requirements.title: Fall 2026 entrant credit policy and repeat forfeiture
requirements.summary: This gateway expressly applies only to Fall 2026 entrants (Class of 2030), not automatically to every 6-4_2025 cohort. Entrance credit may be equivalent-subject or unrestricted elective credit at departmental discretion; S credits do not enter GPA. Registering for any version of a subject already credited from prior study forfeits that credit; reinstatement requires dropping by Add Date. Earlier entrants need their own cohort policy.

requirements.title: Optional HASS field: Computing and Society
requirements.summary: This is one optional HASS concentration, not an AI-major requirement or the only eligible HASS field. Apply its child rule only when this field is selected. Other HASS fields retain their own advisor-approved requirements.

requirements.title: Four advisor-selected subjects
requirements.summary: For this chosen HASS field, complete four listed subjects in consultation with its advisor. At most one may also meet the HASS Distribution requirement. Topic-specific special-subject titles are preserved rather than treating every offering of a special number as eligible.

requirements.title: Linked Course 18 similarity restrictions
requirements.summary: The linked mathematics page labels its new program Fall 2026+ and directs earlier entrants to older rules; special subjects are not automatically eligible. Its similarity exclusions allow at most one within each set: {18.06, 18.C06, 18.700}; {18.702, 18.703}; {18.04, 18.075, 18.112}; {18.05, 18.600, 6.3700, 15.069, 15.079}; {18.650, 15.075}; {18.400J, 18.404J}; {18.062, 18.200, 18.200A}; {18.413, 18.417}. The 6-4 source explicitly applies the no-similar-content criterion to its open MATH elective. Historical special cases remain restricted to their stated offerings; these groups are exclusions, not a finite elective pool.

requirements.title: Advanced Placement: math science
requirements.summary: For Fall 2026 entrants only, AP Calculus BC 5 earns 18.01; AB 5 permits accelerated 18.01A/18.02A placement rather than credit. Both Physics C exams at 5 earn 8.01. No AP Biology, Chemistry, Computer Science, Environmental Science, Statistics or separate Physics 1/2 credit is granted. Lower scores receive no partial credit; a repeated exam uses the higher score.

requirements.title: Advanced Placement: electives
requirements.summary: For the stated entrant cohort, eligible Arts, English, History/Social Sciences and World Languages/Cultures AP exams at 5 yield nine unrestricted elective units each. Both Capstone exams at 5 together yield nine units. AP never substitutes for HASS; English AP placement does not waive the first-year CI subject. Official College Board scores, rather than self-reports, establish credit.

requirements.title: International Examinations: math physics
requirements.summary: Within the Fall-2026-entry policy gateway, A-level Mathematics/Physics A* or A earn 18.01/8.01; higher-level IB Mathematics/Physics 7 earn those respective subjects. Pre-U Physics D1/D2/D3 earns 8.01, while Pre-U Mathematics/Further Mathematics earns none. French Baccalaureate Mathematics/Physics 16–20 and Abitur Mathematics/Physics 13–15 earn 18.01/8.01 respectively. Unlisted examinations require departmental review.

requirements.title: International Examinations: other
requirements.summary: The listed qualifying humanities/arts/social-science international exams earn nine unrestricted elective units: A-level A*/A, higher-level IB 7, Pre-U D1–D3, French Baccalaureate 16–20 or Abitur 13–15. Geography A*/A is listed for three unrestricted units in A-level and Pre-U sections. The source denies Biology/Chemistry credit across its listed systems and specified A-level CS/IB ITGS credit. Final degree credit needs official final certification (or electronically released IB results), not preliminary results alone. The gateway limits these policies to its entrant cohort.
